rationale: `decorates` was the vb lane's missing type: the grammar makes an attribute list a DECLARATION's child (field("attributes", $.attribute_list) on every declaration production), and the analyzer suppressed attribute-position names from `references` after a differential finding, so 202 attribute sites over the 58-file admitted population published NOTHING — neither an edge nor a count. The emission added for this fixture publishes `decorates <declaration> -> <attribute leaf>` from pushSymbol, which is the one place every published symbol passes through, so no visitor can forget it. THE TARGET IS THE LEAF ON PURPOSE: the arbiter binds by name against the project's declarations, so `System.Serializable` is unresolvable by construction while `Serializable` resolves exactly when the project declares its own attribute type; rust's ruling for this type, applied to this grammar. THE FIELD CASE IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: `_a, _b As Integer` is ONE field_declaration with TWO declarators, and the symbol for each is published from the DECLARATOR — so the attribute holder is resolved by climbing to the declaration, bounded to field_declaration/declaration_statement so a member can never inherit its enclosing type's attributes.

expectRelationships.comment: A type attribute with an argument. The source is the DECLARATION it decorates, and the target is the leaf (`Obsolete`, never `System.Obsolete`) so the arbiter can bind it.

THE DECLARATOR CLIMB. `_a` and `_b` are two symbols published from two variable_declarators of ONE field_declaration, and the attribute list lives on the declaration. Both rows are required: an emission that read only the declarator would publish neither, and one that emitted once per declaration would publish only the first.
The second declarator of the same field, for the reason above.
A method attribute whose ARGUMENT is itself a qualified name (`EditorBrowsableState.Never`). The argument must not be read as a second attribute — see the forbid row below.
A property attribute with NO argument list. The bare `<Obsolete>` form is the one an argument-count assumption would drop.
A QUALIFIED attribute name: the written spelling is `System.Serializable` and the published target is its leaf. This is the row that fails if the emission keeps the full spelling as the target.
the QUALIFIED-GLOBAL attribute name still decorates the declaration; the written spelling lives in metadata.attributeName

forbidRelationships.comment: THE ARGUMENT IS NOT AN ATTRIBUTE. `EditorBrowsableState.Never` is the attribute's ARGUMENT; publishing it as a decoration would make one syntactic event two edges and put a type-use name where an applied attribute belongs.

THE SUPPRESSION THIS FIXTURE MUST NOT UNDO. Attribute-position names are deliberately absent from `references` (the lane's differential reported them as unexplained rows, and `inAttributePosition` is that ruling). `decorates` publishes the construct; re-enabling the value read would double-count the same site on a second edge type.

THE UNBOUNDED-CLIMB DEFECT. `Keep` is a member of `Store`, which is decorated; if the holder climb were unbounded, `Keep` would inherit `<System.Serializable()>` from its enclosing type. The bounded climb exists for exactly this row.

THE QUALIFIED-CHAIN ARGUMENT IS NOT A READ. `Global.System.ComponentModel.EditorBrowsableState.Advanced` is an attribute ARGUMENT: the compiler reads it, the decorated declaration does not. Measured on DISMTools' generated Settings.Designer.vb:31, where the old inAttributePosition climb stopped at the first member_access_expression and published this row (3 unexplained uses per 60-file draw).
same shape, the qualified type half of the argument
same shape, the namespace half of the argument
an attribute argument is not a type reference either — the same ruling the bare-argument forbid above records
